papers_read.title_as_printed: Pack file pdf/P-114.txt is the San-Martin et al. EEG/LORETA paper (BSPC 66 (2021) 102499), P-112's paper. The paper the record means (claim '93% Acc', registry row Kinect/ANFIS gait, summaries.md header 1-s2.0-S1746809421003195) is Seifallahi et al., 'Detection of mild cognitive Impairment from gait using Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference system', BSPC 71 (2022) 103195, present in the pack as pdf/P-115.txt. Both read in full; verdict uses the gait paper.

Analysis of neuropsychological and neuroradiological features for diagnosis of Alzheimer's disease and mild cognitive impairment (Kurbalija et al., International Journal of Medical Informatics 178 (2023) 105195)

what_each_reports.P-114: Kinect V2 dual-task gait features, 150 older adults (70 MCI, 80 HC, Tehran), hierarchical ANFIS binary MCI vs HC accuracy 93%; evaluation protocol for ANFIS not stated.
what_each_reports.P-95: 90 participants (30 AD, 30 MCI, 30 healthy; Novi Sad), 482 neuropsychological and neuroradiological features, seven Weka classifiers with default settings, 10x10 stratified CV, THREE-CLASS AD/MCI/control classification. All-attribute accuracy ranged 66.22% (LR) to 81.00% (naive Bayes); weighted-average AUROC 76.3% to 95.0%. Best expert-selected NP combination 79.78% (SVM, A3). NR-only feature groups mostly below 50% accuracy.

quantity_a: Accuracy of ANFIS on gait features, binary MCI vs healthy controls, protocol unstated
quantity_b: Accuracy (range across seven classifiers) of three-class AD vs MCI vs control classification from neuropsychological tests plus MRI/DTI measures, 10x10 stratified CV
incompatible_if_same: No. A three-class accuracy is bounded differently from a binary one (chance 33% vs 50%), and P-95's figure is a range across classifiers, not one estimate; neither paper claims an ordering the other refutes.

gates.task: mismatch: P-114 binary MCI vs HC (T1); P-95 three-class AD/MCI/control (the registry codes P-95 as T3)
gates.dataset_family: mismatch: own IDAA Tehran cohort vs own University Clinical Centre of Vojvodina cohort; no waiver
gates.validation_tier: uncertain: P-95 internal 10x10 stratified CV; P-114 protocol unstated
gates.modality_family: mismatch: gait/motor vs neuropsychological test battery plus structural/diffusion MRI; no waiver

endpoint_and_metric: incompatible: binary accuracy vs three-class accuracy range
performance_validity: flag does not apply: neither row flagged; P-95's 95.0% weighted AUROC is below 0.97 and is not the contested figure.
independence: Independent: different groups and cohorts; no shared authors.
grounds: P-95's 66-81% is the accuracy range of seven classifiers on a three-class AD/MCI/control task, while P-114's 93% is a binary MCI-vs-HC accuracy, so the class contrast and endpoint differ.
The predictor sets differ entirely: P-95 uses 482 neuropsychological and neuroradiological attributes (including MMSE and ACE III, which enter the diagnosis), P-114 uses Kinect gait parameters.
The task gate, modality-family gate and dataset-family gate all fail with no waiver on record.

evidence_quotes.quote: the proposed ANFIS classifier had values of 93%, 90%, and 91.5% for accuracy, sensitivity, and F-score, respectively when all extracted gait parameters in the DTW condition for the classification of elderly subjects to MCI and HC groups.
The accuracy for the whole set of attributes ranged between 66.22 % and 81.00 %, and the weighted average AUROC was between 76.3 % and 95.0 %.
the application of machine learning techniques in AD diagnosis will be directed toward the creation of ML classifiers which will be trained to perform the 3-class classification.
The data for this study consists of NP and NR features (as explained in Section 3) for 30 patients with AD, 30 patients with MCI and 30 healthy individuals

record_defects: The pack's P-114 PDF (paper_pdf_map.json, 'formula-unverified') is P-112's EEG paper, not the gait/ANFIS paper the record means.
claim_b 'P-95: 66-81% on T1' mislabels a three-class AD/MCI/control accuracy range as a T1 result.
task_equal, dataset_equal and validation_comparable 'Yes' are wrong or unsupported.
The resolution note's reason ('Metric type unclear') is incomplete: P-95 states the metric (accuracy) clearly; the pair fails on task, modality and cohort.
what_would_change_the_verdict: Nothing in these papers: P-95 reports no binary MCI-vs-control accuracy.
